title: Phase 1b: sample-at-existing-grid backfill of beat_refiner sigmoid confidences
description:
Follow-up to LiveChord-sfw (Phase 1, commit 286040b). Backfill beat_probs[]/downbeat_probs[] for the ~25% rejected-at-ingest corpus by sampling raw sigmoid frames at existing beats[]/downbeats[] timestamps instead of re-peak-picking (which causes SKIP_LENGTH_MISMATCH).

Design:
- Extract _extract_sigmoid_frames() helper from refine() (audio decode + model forward, returns raw per-frame sigmoid arrays)
- Add public sample_probs_at_grid(audio_path, beats, downbeats) — does NOT peak-pick, samples at given timestamps via nearest-frame lookup (round(t * FRAMES_PER_SEC), clamped to [0, T-1])
- tools/backfill_beat_probs.py: add --mode grid (default), --force-overwrite-peak-pick guard
- process_queue.py: stamp prob_source='peak_pick' on Phase 1 ingest, clear on bar_arbitrator wipe, wire (but don't enable) ingest hook for rejected songs behind beat_refiner_sample_on_reject settings flag
- Top-level chord_data['prob_source'] field: 'peak_pick' | 'sample_at_grid' | absent (legacy)
- 6 new sampler tests + 2 splitter tests covering sample_at_grid path

Scope: backfill-only, ingest hook OFF by default. Plan file: C:\Users\hitea\.claude\plans\phase-1b-misty-hearth.md
notes:
Backfill complete 2026-05-17. Actual results departed substantially from plan estimate.

Backfill summary (--mode grid --workers 4, elapsed 75s):
- Queued: 53,945 chord JSONs
- OK: 29 (mode=grid wrote beat_probs/downbeat_probs/prob_source)
- SKIP_NO_BEATS: 53,916 (99.95%)
- SKIP_LENGTH_MISMATCH: 0 (Phase 1b worked as designed)
- FAIL: 0

- 98.5% are 'source: btc_batch' (or btc/midi) with chords[] populated but beats[]=downbeats=[]
  — these are pre-beat-tracker ingests from the 2026-04 GPU batch
- 1.4% (27/2000) have beats[]+downbeats[] AND already have nprob>0 (Phase 1 covered)
- Zero songs in the sample had beats[]+downbeats[] WITHOUT existing peak_pick probs

So the "rejected at gate 4" cohort Phase 1b targets is genuinely tiny — only the 29 OK songs match. Phase 1b is correct as built, but its actual coverage gain is small.

Real corpus gap (out of scope for Phase 1b):
- The 53k+ btc_batch songs need beat tracking populated FIRST. That's LiveChord-g1k
  "Admin tool: identify songs with degenerate beat data and bulk-trigger upgrade".

3. Bulk POST to existing /api/process/beats/switch?mode=madmom for each (queues sequentially via beat_upgrade_queue)
4. Status polling shows progress

title: Phase 1: propagate beat_refiner sigmoid confidences to chord_splitter for prob-weighted bar-snap
description:
Currently beat_refiner emits per-frame sigmoid probabilities (beat_logits, downbeat_logits at beat_refiner_infer.py:284-285) but they're discarded after _peak_pick. Only binary times[] propagate to chord_splitter.

Goal: persist per-bar downbeat probability alongside bars[] so chord_splitter can weight bar-snap decisions. High-confidence bars trigger snap; low-confidence bars leave chord onsets as-is (preserves real off-bar chord changes).

Implementation outline:
1. Modify _peak_pick at beat_refiner_infer.py:167 to return (times[], probs[]) instead of just times[]
2. Persist beat_probs[] / downbeat_probs[] alongside beats[] / downbeats[] in chord JSON
3. global_chord_arbiter._compound_6_8_meter_info derives bars[] AND bar_probs[] (averaged from constituent downbeat_probs)
4. chord_splitter._compound_six_eight_bar_snap (the Phase 0 function) gates snap on bar_prob >= threshold (e.g. 0.7)

Caveat: beat_refiner is REJECTED for many songs (e.g. A Thousand Years case: refiner score 0.58 < beat_this score 0.60 → applied=false). Songs without refiner output have no probs. Either:
(a) Run refiner anyway when not better, persist probs but don't replace times[]
(b) Backfill a synthetic 'beats from beat_this' confidence proxy (e.g. uniform 0.5)

Recommend (a) for first iteration.

Backfill: re-run refiner over the corpus to populate probs (additive schema change).

SESSION HANDOFF — branch: feature/ai-accompaniment-styles, last commit b5244f8.

## Reproduction
1. Open any song with Guitar tab as default (or switch mid-playback piano→guitar).
2. Use AI Accompaniment with style=PopBallad or any arpeggio-mode style.
3. Watch waterfall: bass thumb (p) appears at beat ~2.5 visually
4. Listen: bass note plays correctly on beat 1.
5. Verified ✅ on http://192.168.50.6:8800/player?path=...Cupid... (key D, BPM 120)

## Critical files (read before touching)
- [frontend/js/string-instrument.js:336-398](frontend/js/string-instrument.js#L336) — _generateRhEvents arpeggio path
- [frontend/js/string-instrument.js:400-430](frontend/js/string-instrument.js#L400) — _drawRhWaterfall (calls _generateRhEvents)
- [frontend/js/arpeggio-patterns.js](frontend/js/arpeggio-patterns.js) — pima/pimami/pami/pima_chord/travis/folk/pop_ballad pattern definitions
- [frontend/js/player.js:6481](frontend/js/player.js#L6481) — scheduleNotes audio scheduler (consumes accData.right_hand)
- [frontend/js/player.js:_resolveRhEvents](frontend/js/player.js) — RH event resolver, respects rhContentMode
- [backend/ai/accompaniment_generator.py _build_right_hand](backend/ai/accompaniment_generator.py) — backend RH generator (engine v5 period-tile)

## Why this matters
After my engine v5 period-tile fix (commit 95e62a3), audio events tile at fixed beat-period from chord.time → bar-aware. Guitar visual still uses cycleDur from chord.time. For 4-beat chords starting on bar boundary they coincide; for 2-beat chords or chords on offbeats they diverge.

## Three fix options (choose one in next session)

**Option A — visual→audio**: map _generateRhEvents events to MIDI pitches via the chord diagram (strings[s].fret + open-string MIDI). Replace audio-side accData.right_hand consumption when on guitar/uke tab with the local generator output. Pros: visual always wins. Cons: loses backend's velocity humanization, melody-gap awareness.

**Option B — audio→visual**: _drawRhWaterfall consumes accData.right_hand. Map each piano-pitch event to nearest guitar string (lossy — multiple pitches → same string collide). Lose the strum/pick semantics. Pros: minimal code change. Cons: visual doesn't look like a guitar anymore.

**Option C — backend extension**: STYLE_CONFIG gets style_family field. When 'string', _build_right_hand emits {type, strings, finger, time, dur} events. Synth playback path unchanged (still uses pitch). Add a string→pitch resolver on synth side. Pros: cleanest, audio + visual share source. Cons: backend cache schema bump (engine v5→v6), most code changed.

**Recommended: C** — biggest investment, lowest long-term tech debt. Visual + audio share one truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- Guitar visual + MIDI audio arpeggio events fire at IDENTICAL absolute times for any chord+style combination.
- Switching tab mid-playback (piano→guitar) doesn't introduce a phase offset.
- Existing piano tab behavior unchanged.
- Existing accordion/arranger tabs unchanged (they consume accData directly via the keyboard waterfall, no _generateRhEvents).

## Out of scope for this issue
- Pattern-set design (pima/folk/etc) — keep as-is, just unify the rendering source.
- Velocity / humanization — engine v5 already handles this on audio side.
- LH side — no divergence reported.

## How to confirm before merging
- Playwright: open Cupid.flac, AI Acc style=Auto, switch to guitar, advance to second beat of measure 2, getBoundingClientRect of the bottom-most strum bar should match floor(audio.currentTime * pxPerSec) within 1px.
- Manual: ear-test piano vs guitar accompaniment on the same song — should sound IDENTICAL note-for-note.
